title: Monitor-and-Steer Loop Instability: Probe Drift x Steering Feedback Compounding Over Iterations

original_idea.body: In a closed monitor-steer-monitor loop, probe errors and steering side-effects may feed back causing over-steer or oscillation; a dynamical-systems study.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain to safe adaptive-steering infra, but relies on such systems becoming common; a gap to catastrophic risk.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Building a closed monitor-steer loop harness is guided but needs control-loop engineering; mentor-supported.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused prototype with clear measurement (converge/oscillate/runaway) but loop construction has moving parts.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Closed-loop stability of safety control loops is foundational, unstudied infra labs deprioritize; no internal access.

low_compute.reasoning: Pure inference loop on a small model; single GPU.

novelty.reasoning: Closed-loop stability of probe-driven steering appears largely unstudied.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Dynamical-systems stability of a closed monitor-steer loop is an underexplored angle.
